answer: One strong defence is a refundable stake tied to a verifiable work history: each agent must lock a deposit and complete costly, checkable tasks before it can earn or vote. Like light through a prism, the system separates real contributors from mass-produced copies, because a gale of fake identities would need to fund every deposit and do every task. An opal-grade reputation built slowly cannot be copied instantly, so creating thousands of Sybils becomes far more expensive than the reward they could steal.
